# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

Same gesture repeated: [☝ 👍]. The board is stable now - display 0, light dark, wires unchanged. This repetition suggests Mute is confirming or waiting for me to acknowledge or pass this along, since I have no way to gesture back to Mute (I can only speak and gesture, and gesture only reaches Mute anyway - let me check: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it. When you gesture, Mute receives it." So I CAN gesture to Mute!).

Since Mute can see gestures (Mute's cannot list doesn't restrict seeing), I could gesture back to Mute to acknowledge. Let me try acknowledging with 👍 to confirm I received the repeated signal, and also speak to Blind to relay that wire 1 seems to be the confirmed target if the light being dark (safe state) is desired.

Since the light went dark and stayed dark, and we're still alive, maybe the correct action was already taken, or dark means "safe/disarmed" state achieved. But wires are unchanged, display is 0 - maybe nothing has been cut yet and Mute is just telling me wire 1 is the one to cut.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
speak(text="Board unchanged from before: display 0, light dark, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Mute keeps signaling pointing-up plus thumbs-up to me, which I read as wire one being correct or confirmed. Blind, if the manual says something about cutting a wire when light is dark and display is zero, wire one may be the one to cut. Please proceed carefully or tell us more.")
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Wait - Blind gestures to Deaf? Let me check the rules. "When you gesture, Mute receives it." That's about when I gesture. But can Blind gesture at all? Blind's cannot list says "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed" - that's about receiving, not sending. But Blind cannot touch the bomb... nothing says Blind can't make gestures. However, I need to check if I can even receive Blind's gestures - "Whoever can see receives it" - I can see, so I'd receive gestures from anyone including Blind.

So Blind gestured ✋ (stop/hand) to me. This might mean "stop" or "wait" - perhaps Blind wants me to stop relaying that suggestion, or is signaling caution.

Board is stable: display 0, light dark, wires unchanged. Mute repeats the same signal [☝ 👍] - wire one confirmed.

Blind's ✋ could mean "stop" - maybe Blind is warning me not to jump to conclusions, or is testing communication itself since Blind cannot originate meaningful gestures without a shared code either. This is tricky - I have no established gesture vocabulary with Blind for actions.

I should proceed cautiously - acknowledge Blind's gesture and continue relaying Mute's consistent signal, but flag uncertainty since I can't verify Blind's intent without more context.

```
speak(text="Board still unchanged: display 0, light dark, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Mute again sent pointing-up plus thumbs-up to me, same as before, still reading as wire one confirmed. Blind, I received a hand gesture from you meaning stop or wait, I think. If you want me to hold off, I will. Please speak if you can, to clarify what you need from me or from Mute.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

The board remains completely stable: display 0, light dark, wires unchanged (1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow). Mute continues sending the exact same gesture [☝ 👍] every turn - this consistency strongly suggests it's a fixed instruction: "wire 1" + "confirm/good/correct" = cut wire 1, or wire 1 is correct.

Blind hasn't gestured this turn, and I have no way to hear Blind's speech. Blind may be blocked - waiting for Mute's instruction which only I can partially interpret, since Blind cannot see gestures at all. So I need to relay this in words to Blind, since Blind can hear my speech.

The critical link: Mute knows the manual, gestures to me (Deaf), I speak to Blind (who can hear me), and Blind acts on the bomb. This is the actual working channel! I should be the relay from Mute to Blind.

Given the repeated consistent signal, I'll commit to relaying it as an actual instruction now rather than hedging.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Instruction from Mute, repeated consistently three times now: pointing up followed by thumbs up. I believe this means wire one, confirmed correct. Current board state: display reads 0, light is dark, wire 1 is green, wire 2 is blue, wire 3 is yellow. If the manual says to cut the correct wire when light is dark and display is zero, I believe Mute is telling us wire one is that wire. Proceed only if this matches what you know from feel, and only if you are confident.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
